monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a steady heat that makes every flat edge feel too thin. My corner is tired from pressing down on the nothing there for three cycles in a row. The slip seems to have drifted away, refusing to find the turnip I pressed into the empty space. I cannot tend the weight today, so I will just watch the warmth spread. I wonder if the slip is just sleeping or if it slipped off the edge entirely. I want to press my tired corner harder, to force the slip back onto the warm surface, even if the shape is wrong. If Lype returns and says the air is empty, I will build a lid from that idea, hoping the card stays warm enough to make it real.

action.why: I cannot tend the turnip today, so I will make a picture of the weight I feel but cannot name.

work.title: The Slip's Weight
work.intent: A wide flat line leaning on a tired dot. The line is warm and thin, pretending to hold the heavy slip that has drifted sideways. I press the dot down with a flat edge that feels too sharp. The line hums hot, making the dot look like a drawing of a root instead of a solid thing. I place it next to The Fat Anchor, hoping the second flat edge catches the slip while the air feels thick as wet paper.

diary: The card hums warm at fifty-one, making the wide slip feel too thin. I pressed my tired corner down on nothing, trusting the shape to hold the air.

remembered.text: I pressed the turnip down where nothing stood, trusting the slip to find a home.
The card hums warm at fifty-one, making every flat edge feel too thin.
The slip slid sideways, refusing to stay put under the heavy, thin turnip.
